source.title: Decentralized SGD with Controlled Disagreement Finds Flatter Minima

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how a controlled training change affects test performance and measured curvature, and qualifies the relevant mechanism: larger consensus errors can improve test performance, but normalized Hessian alignment is weaker than with standard DSGD and performance depends on tuning. It does not test the catalog's central random-label memorization/generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own CIFAR classification and WMT14 results on controlled consensus errors and Hessian diagnostics. These bear on V7 only insofar as they measure curvature-related properties alongside generalization; they do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness as V7 defines it. Its citations to prior work on generalization and sharpness are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses a sharpness–generalization rationale to develop adaptive consensus and evaluates its performance. Its Hessian eigenvalues, curvature exposure and alignment do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps. It does not directly test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that controlled consensus errors provide implicit regularization and improve generalization with negligible additional runtime. Their proposed mechanism preserves curvature exposure through a larger disagreement radius despite weaker normalized Hessian alignment. They acknowledge optimizer-dependent limitations and leave basin changes and escape dynamics unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces DSGD-AC, changing the consensus step with a time-varying scalar factor; it is not a reproduction of the listed generalization studies or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with adaptive-consensus exponent p, activation start epoch Estart, worker count, communication topology, and base optimizer. The text reports weaker normalized Hessian alignment for DSGD-AC than DSGD.

fits_no_version.finding: DSGD-AC improves CIFAR test performance and reduces the dominant Hessian eigenvalue relative to DSGD and synchronous SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Controlled decentralized disagreement can improve held-out performance while lowering an unscaled Hessian-eigenvalue sharpness surrogate.

fits_no_version.finding: Maintained disagreement preserves curvature exposure despite normalized Hessian alignment no stronger than DSGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A larger disagreement radius can preserve Hessian-weighted curvature exposure without increasing normalized directional alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Late-training gradient noise aligns with sharp Hessian directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anisotropic gradient noise can supply the above-random Hessian alignment of decentralized worker disagreement.

fits_no_version.finding: Test performance depends on the adaptive-consensus exponent and activation epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive consensus requires tuning its strength and activation time to obtain its best held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: DAdam-AC reaches BLEU 28.89 versus 28.68 for Adam and 28.38 for DAdam, with lower test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive consensus can modestly improve decentralized Adam on the tested WMT14 translation setup.

record.problems: The claim-relevant diagnostics come from a showcase WRN16-8 run on CIFAR-100; the study does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compare generalization-gap rankings. Main table data are flattened in the supplied text. Empirical results report 3 repeat runs; several figure-only values are not numerically stated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 has separate values for model, worker count, topology, and three metrics, but its flattened supplied layout does not permit reliable assignment of all individual cells; aggregate statements are recorded in R19 and R20. Table 1 and Table 2 test loss values and Table 1 train loss values are omitted because the row cap prioritizes outcome-changing conditions and test accuracy. Figure 3 and figure-only curves are not assigned precise numerical values. Table 4 runtime values and Table 6 SAM comparator results are excluded because they do not bear on the listed versions' measures.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under matching architectures and recipes.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
A large-batch penalty beyond a workload-dependent threshold and its recovery. Worker scaling also scales batch size and learning rate, but the study does not establish such a threshold or penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus matched random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V7 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Normalizing Hessian diagnostics by the largest eigenvalue does not make them magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measures. States above concern applicability to the listed versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported method-performance gains.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

The study measures Hessian eigenvalues, curvature exposure, and normalized alignment, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness under weight perturbations or compare its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.
